decision: held: freshness search revises conclusion — the credited 'testosterone' supported outcome (26791805, abstract-only) is not reproduced by the same-preparation RCT 31828857 (Testofen 600 mg/day for 12 weeks in men aged 45-80: testosterone and free testosterone unchanged) and is rated very low certainty with no stable free-testosterone effect by 42688439 (2026 SR/MA, which rejects testosterone-boosting claims). Before any Testofen credit is kept, this must be reconciled against 31828857's full text and the 2020 Testofen exercise trial, including whether credit narrows to the AMS symptom outcome.
summary: 26791805 (120 healthy men aged 43-70, Testofen seed extract 600 mg/day for 12 weeks) met its primary outcome (lower Aging Male Symptom score) and improved sexual function and total/free testosterone versus placebo. 21312304 tested Testofen within a mineral formulation and is recorded without credit. Dr. Pham's date-restricted hold had its age-only exclusion withdrawn; credit is scoped to Testofen in healthy older men, with abstract-only verification noted. Fourth-ruling boundary applied: fertility, erectile, hypogonadism and muscle-growth positioning excluded. A 2026-10-28 freshness search found a second Testofen RCT with unchanged testosterone and a 2026 meta-analysis rating testosterone evidence very low certainty, so the credit decision is held for reconciliation.

freshness_search.database: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esearch, sort=pub_date, retmax=60; titles via esummary, abstracts via efetch)
freshness_search.query: (fenugreek OR "Trigonella foenum-graecum" OR Testofen) AND (testosterone OR androgen OR "aging male" OR libido OR sexual) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR randomized controlled trial[pt])
freshness_search.screening_rule: Kept syntheses of fenugreek and testosterone or male symptoms, and RCTs in men. Excluded women-only and menopause trials, and combination drinks with PDE5 inhibitors. Testofen identity of 31828857 was taken from the study table of 42688439 (full text), because that trial's abstract does not name the brand.

read.title: Effects of oral fenugreek-derived preparations on testosterone-related outcomes in adult men: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
read.finding: 2026 SR/MA (searched to May 11, 2026; PMC full text read), 13 RCTs: total testosterone SMD 0.25 (0.02 to 0.48; 6 studies, I2 0%), free testosterone SMD 0.08 (-0.48 to 0.63; 5 studies, I2 66.7%). Certainty is very low for both, and no included study had low risk of bias. The review concludes the evidence does not support testosterone-boosting claims. Its study table lists 26791805 as the core Testofen study, plus two more Testofen RCTs: 31828857 (BPH) and Rao-Mallard-Grant 2020 (exercising men, high risk of bias).

read.title: The effect of Trigonella foenum-graecum extract on prostate-specific antigen, and prostate function in otherwise healthy men with benign prostate hyperplasia.
read.finding: 2020 RCT, 100 men aged 45-80 with BPH symptoms, 600 mg/day fenugreek extract (Testofen per 42688439 Table 1) for 12 weeks. IPSS (primary) did not improve. Testosterone, free testosterone, SHBG and PSA were unchanged.

read.title: Effect of a plant extract of fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) on testosterone in blood plasma and saliva in a double blind randomized controlled intervention study.
read.finding: 2024 RCT of a different preparation (TrigozimR with nutrients), 95 men aged 40-80, 12 weeks: plasma total testosterone and free testosterone index did not rise vs placebo; saliva testosterone did. No subjective effects.

read.title: The Anabolic Effect of Fenugreek: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
read.finding: 2023 MA, 7 studies (449, mainly male athletes): total testosterone SMD 0.32 (0.09 to 0.55); free testosterone SMD 0.24 (-0.04 to 0.52), not significant.

read.title: Effect of fenugreek extract supplement on testosterone levels in male: A meta-analysis of clinical trials.
read.finding: 2020 MA of 4 trials: fenugreek extract had a significant effect on total serum testosterone. The abstract gives no effect size.

read.title: Efficacy of fenugreek seed extract on men's psychological and physical health: a randomized placebo-controlled double-blind clinical trial.
read.finding: 2020 RCT, 57 healthy men (mean age 26), fenugreek extract 400-500 mg/day (preparation not named) for 60 days: aging-male symptoms, anxiety, grip strength and HRQoL improved vs placebo. No hormone outcomes in the abstract.

freshness_search.conclusion: revises: the newest and largest synthesis rates testosterone outcomes at very low certainty, with no stable free-testosterone benefit, and rejects testosterone-boosting claims. A second Testofen-specific RCT (31828857: 600 mg/day for 12 weeks in men aged 45-80) found testosterone and free testosterone unchanged. The credited 'testosterone' outcome rests on one industry-funded trial (26791805, abstract-only) that the same-preparation evidence does not reproduce. Its AMS symptom result is not directly contradicted.
